One evening, a young spirit named Lyra caught a jar of golden fireflies from the terrestrial meadows. She climbed the highest mountain peak and threw them into the reach of the heavens. The fireflies did not vanish; they clung to the velvet, burning with a soft, persistent glow. The Moon was delighted, witnessing the birth of the first stars. She decreed that these tiny lanterns would guide the lost and watch over the dreaming souls below.

However, the Sun grew jealous of this newfound beauty. He cast his harsh, golden rays to burn them away each morning. But the fireflies were resilient, hiding in the hidden pockets of the atmosphere until the Sun retreated. Thus, the dance began—an eternal cycle of emergence and concealment. Tonight, look up; those flickering diamonds are not merely gas or fire, but the original embers of Lyra’s gift, keeping their quiet vigil over our restless, spinning world.
